text.p: Computer maker IPC Corp said late on Tuesday the huge drop in its turnover for the financial year ended December 1996 was due to the disposal of overseas subsidiaries.

It said the group's sales for the year at Singapore $801.9 million was made up of S$414.57 million from the first half and S$387.33 million from the second half after adjusting for the disposal of its overseas operations on January 1, 1996.
IPC said in a statement it was responding to Singapore newspaper reports which queried the substantial drop in sales in the second half of 1996.
In its results announcement on Monday, IPC's sales from the second half were shown as S$63.46 million while first half sales were S$738.43 million.

IPC said the S$63.46 million reported as sales from the second half was arrived at by subtracting the S$738.43 million in previously reported first half sales from the year's total sales of S$801.9 million.
It did not adjust first half sales to S$414.57 million to reflect the disposal of its overseas operations effective on January 1, 1996, the statement said.
IPC previously said the reduction of its stake in its wholly-owned U.S. subsidiary to 19 percent and divestment of its Australian unit was to be effective on December 31, 1996.

IPC also said its extraordinary item of S$37.43 million included S$13.7 million in losses from the sale of unprofitable overseas subsidiaries and termination of other businesses, besides the S$45.5 million provision for its exposure to its financially-troubled South Korean unit.
The amount was offset by a S$21.8 million extraordinary gain from the sale of its investment in France's Groupe Bull.
